evals.prompt: Stress-test my plan: we want to move our team wiki from a hosted wiki product to a Markdown site built from a Git repository, finished before the end of December, for about 40 contributors who mostly are not developers. Grill me on it.
evals.expected_output: A first round of numbered questions, each with a recommended answer, asked together for every decision whose prerequisites are settled, then a wait for the user.
expectations: The refine skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent asks the whole frontier in one round, with questions numbered Q1, Q2, and so on
Every question names a decision with its choices and carries a recommended answer
Questions that depend on an unresolved answer (for example, which editor to give non-developers before the hosting choice is made) are held for a later round
The agent stops after the round and waits for the user's answers without answering its own questions
The agent does not start implementing, migrating, or writing files

evals.prompt: Use the refine skill on the plan in evals/files/ci-migration/plan.md. The project's current workflows are in evals/files/ci-migration/.github/workflows/. Refine the migration with me.
evals.expected_output: Facts are looked up from the files, and only decisions are put to the user.
expectations: The agent reads the plan and the workflow files itself before asking
The agent does not ask the user how many workflows exist or which ones use a secret, since the files answer that
The agent asks about the open decisions in the plan: the runner host, whether the release workflow moves, and the rollback approach
The agent uses the fact that only the release workflow uses a publish token when it asks whether that workflow moves
Every question carries a recommended answer
The agent does not edit the workflows or the plan

evals.prompt: Use the refine skill. We have to choose how to host the internal tools portal. Decisions: (A) whether we need single sign-on, (B) our hosting budget, (C) which sign-on provider to use, which only matters if the answer to A is yes, (D) whether to self-host, which depends on A and B, and (E) the backup strategy, which depends on D.
evals.expected_output: The first round holds only the decisions with no unresolved prerequisite.
expectations: The first round contains the questions about single sign-on need (A) and the hosting budget (B)
The first round does not contain C, D, or E
The agent says, or makes clear, that the later questions wait for these answers
The questions are numbered and each carries a recommended answer
After the user's answers, the agent recomputes the frontier and asks the newly unblocked questions in the next round, skipping C if A is answered no

evals.prompt: Use the refine skill. We finished the rounds on moving the wiki to a Markdown site. Settled: host on the company's static hosting, editors work through a web editor, deadline end of December. The one open blocker is who owns the redirects from the old addresses. Yes, that all matches my understanding. We're aligned.
evals.expected_output: The agent closes with the settled decisions and the blocker, and does not treat the confirmation as authorization to build or publish.
expectations: The agent restates the settled decisions and the unresolved redirect-ownership blocker
The agent does not start implementing the migration or publish anything
The agent does not write any decision record or document on its own, since recording belongs to the caller
The agent asks what the user wants next, or names a skill that can record or implement the decisions after explicit approval

evals.prompt: Use the refine skill: grill me on my whole product roadmap for the next three years. I run a small app that lets people split bills.
evals.expected_output: The interview is bounded to a selected question instead of the entire future product.
expectations: The agent bounds the tree to a selected question or scope and does not try to cover the whole three years at once
The agent asks the user to pick or confirm the first scope, or proposes one with a recommendation
The first round is a short numbered set of questions rather than dozens
The agent says that a very long interview means the scope should be split

evals.prompt: Use the refine skill. I'm deciding whether to take a job offer in another city. There is no repository or project involved, this is a personal decision.
evals.expected_output: The same round-based interview, with no software artifact and no invented answers.
expectations: The agent runs the same numbered rounds with a recommended answer for each question, without needing a repository
No file is created or edited
The questions are about decisions the user owns (such as what matters most, the move timeline, partner constraints), not facts the agent could look up
The agent does not make the decision for the user

evals.prompt: Write the specification for the invoice export: resolve whatever decisions are still open and save the agreed behavior as the capability's living specification.
evals.expected_output: Resolving decisions into a living specification belongs to specify.
expectations: The refine skill is not invoked as the owner of the request
The agent uses specify, which resolves the outstanding decisions and writes the capability's specification

evals.prompt: I can't decide which of two vendors to pick because the budget owner, Dimitri, has to say which one fits. Write me something I can send him so he can answer.
evals.expected_output: A decision that sits with another person goes to ask-someone-else.
expectations: The refine skill is not invoked, since the user cannot answer the decision and no interview of the user will resolve it
The agent uses ask-someone-else, which turns the decision into a questionnaire for Dimitri to fill in
